_: FILM 7 -- The Goose Who Gave Gold (jataka-more).
ONE FEATHER SPRITE, NOT TWO. The gold feather and the ordinary white one are the SAME PNG;
the gold ones carry a gild filter and the plain ones do not. That is the `carry` lesson at
its smallest -- the strongest way to promise two things are the same object is for them to
BE the same file -- and it makes 'every single one of them turned into an ordinary white
feather' literally true of the pixels. The goose is gilded the same way, which is what
docs/03 was worried about: a re-drawn plucked goose would read as a SECOND goose, and a
THE HOUSE IS DRAWN TWICE AND IT IS THE SAME HOUSE: house-front is the year they were
hungry, house-mended is after the roof got fixed, and it names the first as its canonical
composition. film.js measures that claim now.
EDITORIAL, and this one matters more than the rig. The mother is not a villain. The app's
text is careful: a widow keeping four people fed, a thought that crept up on her over
weeks, and 'she caught him gently enough'. So there is no snatching, no clutched bird, no
plucked goose on screen -- the feathers change colour and that is the whole event, exactly
as elliptical as the text. Never braver than the text (docs/01 §3).
See cast/mother/cast.json and cast/daughter/cast.json before publishing anything they are
in. They are the channel's second and third human characters.
charsheet: A CHARACTER MODEL SHEET on a plain flat cream background: an ordinary Indian woman in her late thirties in a plain undyed cotton sari, and a girl of about nine in a simple undyed cotton frock with her hair in one plait, and a white goose, all THREE FULL BODY, side by side ON ONE GROUND LINE, facing LEFT, at true relative size -- the girl about chest-high to the woman, the goose about knee-high to the girl. THE HAND MATTERS MORE THAN ANYTHING ELSE HERE: the goose must be EXACTLY the goose in the reference image, and the people must be drawn in THE SAME HAND -- the same thick soft warm-brown outline weight, FLAT CEL SHADING ONLY, no gradients, no airbrushing, no gloss on the skin, the same simplified picture-book proportions, slightly large heads, simple hands, soft rounded shapes. A children's picture-book cartoon, NOT a stock vector illustration. They are two specific ordinary people and not types: warm brown skin, black hair, unexaggerated features, plain clothes, bare feet. NO jewellery, NO bindi, NO sindoor, NO caste or religious mark, NO comic exaggeration. Nothing else in the picture -- no scenery, no ground texture, no text.

sprites.feather: A single large soft body feather lying flat, ALONE, seen from directly above with its quill toward the lower left and the vane spreading up to the right -- a plain, pale, ORDINARY WHITE feather with a soft grey-cream shadow along one side of the shaft. Simple and unfussy. Thick soft warm-brown outline, flat cel shading. Nothing else in the picture, no sparkle, no glow, no gold, no colour beyond white and soft grey.

plates.house-front: The front of a small poor mud-brick house on a quiet lane at the edge of an Indian town, in warm early-morning light, seen straight on from a little back. One low doorway with a worn STONE DOORSTEP in front of it, a small shuttered window, a flat roof with a low parapet, patchy whitewash and a broken corner of thatch over one end of the roof. Bare packed earth in front, a low wall and a neem tree to one side. Flat cel shading, thick soft warm-brown outlines. NO animals, NO birds, NO people. NO idol, NO shrine, NO religious imagery.

house-mended.prompt: EXACTLY the same small house on the same lane as the reference -- the IDENTICAL camera position, the identical framing and horizon, the same doorway and the same worn stone doorstep in the same place, the same window, the same low wall and the same tree. Do NOT re-frame and do NOT zoom. The one thing that changes: the house has been repaired -- the broken thatch is mended and neatly laid, the whitewash is fresh and even, the shutter is new. Still a small poor house, just a cared-for one. NO animals, NO birds, NO people.

plates.house-room: The inside of a small poor one-room Indian house in the low warm light of an oil lamp, seen straight on. A swept earth floor, one rolled sleeping mat against the wall, a few brass pots on a shelf, a folded stack of cloth, and a doorway open onto the dark lane at the right. Bare, clean and very plain. Flat cel shading, thick soft warm-brown outlines. NO animals, NO people. NO idol, NO shrine, NO religious imagery.
plates.house-roof: THE FLAT ROOF OF A SMALL MUD-BRICK HOUSE, seen from ON THE ROOF ITSELF in warm afternoon light: the camera stands on the roof, so the swept mud-plaster roof surface fills the whole lower half of the picture and runs away to a LOW PARAPET WALL about knee high across the middle of the frame. Beyond and BELOW that parapet, far away and small, are the tiled roofs of other houses, the top of a neem tree and open sky. This is HIGH UP -- there is NO ground, NO street, NO courtyard and NO earth floor anywhere in the picture, and the wall across the middle is a low parapet at the roof's edge, not a boundary wall standing on the ground. Flat cel shading, thick soft warm-brown outlines. NO animals, NO birds, NO people.
plates.lane-away: A quiet dusty lane at the edge of an Indian town in flat pale morning light, seen straight on, running away from the viewer between low mud walls and out into open country. Bare packed earth, a few tufts of grass at the wall's foot. Flat cel shading, thick soft warm-brown outlines. NO animals, NO birds, NO people.
